KES · deficit-weighted magnitude law · 30 Aug 2026

Lollipop panels: today's default vs the Båth split and two tilted-law variants

Run 00 (seed 42) of four full 3000-yr simulations, each shown in the 1000-yr window that places the run's largest event at 35 %. Stems start at M 5; marker area grows as 3.2M−5, colour is magnitude (plasma). Every panel uses today's fault, loading, stress-shadow and Omori physics; only the magnitude law and event origin differ.

How to read

  • a is the model you had this morning: i.i.d. G-R sizes, aftershocks folded into one rate.
  • b adds the library Båth split: red-edged squares are Omori children, each capped 1.2 below its parent, so the small-event floor after a large event is now visible as a texture.
  • c (μ = 3, κ = 0): sizes track the reservoir. Large events cluster where the fault is full — ρ(Dpre, M | M ≥ 7) = +0.27 over the ensemble vs +0.01 for b — while the rate itself is unchanged.
  • d (μ = 2, κ = 1): the rate also drops when the fault is full, so the decade before the largest event is thinner (M ≥ 5 counts 10 / 9 here; ensemble mean 14.7 / 12.9).
